discovery: Discovery of quantum error correction and the theory of fault-tolerant quantum computation
subfield: Quantum information physics / quantum error correction
motivation: Before 1995 it was widely believed that decoherence made large-scale quantum computation physically impossible, because quantum states cannot be copied and errors are continuous. Shor (1995) and Steane (1996) independently showed that redundant entangled encodings and syndrome measurements can detect and reverse errors without learning the encoded information. Together with the stabilizer formalism, this made a fragile quantum state recoverable. Kitaev's toric and surface codes tied error correction to topological order. They gave a threshold theorem with local, physically realistic operations, and they set the blueprint that now guides every hardware platform. In the last two years superconducting, trapped-ion and neutral-atom experiments have shown logical qubits that improve as code size grows, operating below threshold. This confirms a deep physical prediction: entanglement can protect quantum information against a noisy environment. These ideas created a field and define the path to quantum machines.
